data.name: Patricio
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'patricius', meaning 'nobleman' or 'member of the patrician class'. This title was used in ancient Rome for members of the wealthy and noble families who held high positions within the government. In Christian tradition, the name Patricio honors the early Christian martyrs and saints who sacrificed their lives for their faith and their noble actions.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes courage, nobility, and faith in the face of adversity.
data.numerology_meaning: Patricio is a name with a strong sense of responsibility and nurturing energy. It is a name for those who seek to help others and make a positive impact on the world.

in_hebrew.name: פטריציו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פטריציו הוא שם שמקורו בלטינית, נגזר מהמילה 'פאטר', שפירושה אב או אבות. השם מתייחס לאדם שנולד באצולה, בן לאב אציל. במסורת הנוצרית, השם פטריציו מייצג אדם בעל ייחוס אציל, עם קונוטציות של כבוד, יושרה ומנהיגות.

in_greek.name: Πατρικίος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Πατρικίος είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό 'patricius', που σημαίνει ευγενής ή γεννημένος από ευγενείς. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοιοι όροι χρησιμοποιούνται για να περιγράψουν τους ευγενείς και τους υψηλόβαθμους. Στο πρώιμο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα Πατρικίος συμβόλιζε το κύρος, την αξιοπρέπεια και την πνευματική ηγεσία.

in_latin.name: Patricio
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Patricio originates from the Latin term 'patricius', denoting a patrician or noble. In ancient Rome, patricians were members of the noble class. Early Christian tradition adopted this nomenclature to signify nobility of spirit, moral excellence, and ecclesiastical leadership.

in_english.name: Patricio
in_english.long_meaning: The name Patricio derives from the Latin 'patricius', meaning 'patrician' or 'noble'. It originates from the Roman term for members of the aristocratic class. In Christian tradition, Patricio symbolizes nobility of character, spiritual leadership, and moral integrity. Historically, it has been associated with Saint Patrick, the patron saint of Ireland, although not directly etymologically linked. The name is popular across various Christian cultures, reflecting values of honor and distinction.

data.cultural_impact: The name Patricio takes us back to the roots of the Roman Empire, evoking feelings of nobility, power, and wealth. It also connects us to the historical background of the Christian martyrs and saints, emphasizing the importance and impact of faith while holding a position of power in Roman society.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the name Patricio signifies a person who holds a high position in society but chooses to live their life based on Christian values. It reminds us of the courage and selflessness demonstrated by early Christian martyrs and saints who remained devoted to their faith in the face of adversity and persecution. The name is also a reminder of the importance of using our positions in life to serve and make a positive impact on others and the world.

historical_references.reference: Saint Patricio of Sabina was a 5th century Roman nobleman who became a bishop and a patron saint of Rome. He was born in Sabina, a region in central Italy, and was a nephew of Pope Felix III. Patricio was instrumental in the conversion of the Gauls to Christianity and is considered the Apostle to the Gauls. He is also known as Saint Patrick of Sabina to distinguish him from Saint Patrick of Ireland.
historical_references.context: The conversion of the Gauls to Christianity

historical_references.reference: Saint Patricio de las Escalas was a Spanish saint of the 13th century. He was born in Seville and became a Franciscan friar. Patricio was known for his devotion to the Virgin Mary and is said to have performed many miracles. He was executed during the persecution of the Catholics by the Almohad Caliphate in 1266.
